summary: The second 3D NAND fab of the National Memory Base run by Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) in the East Lake High-tech Zone of Wuhan, China. Construction began on 20 June 2020 with a planned capacity of 200,000 wafers a month, double the first phase. Reports in 2022 expected it to start by the end of that year, but YMTC was placed on the U.S. Entity List in December 2022; trade press in June 2026 said the line formally entered production in 2024 and reached full output of about 60,000 wafers a month within two years. The August 2026 listing prospectus of YMTC's holding company says the main phase 2 line was completed and moved into fixed assets from 2024 and ran at full output in 2025 and early 2026. In April 2026 YMTC's two Wuhan fabs were reported to have a combined capacity of about 200,000 wafers a month.

notes: The prospectus of YMTC's holding company, CCSH Corporation, filed with the Shanghai Stock Exchange in August 2026, is the only primary source found; it reports the phase 2 line's completion, full output and remaining construction in progress (about CNY 2.7 billion on 31 March 2026, with 98.61 percent of the planned project input made) but gives no per-phase capacity, investment, start date or site. A project company for the second phase, set up in December 2021 and owned 70 percent by Hubei Changsheng and 30 percent by China's second national chip fund, was bought by YMTC's holding company in 2023 and merged into Yangtze Memory Technologies in December 2023, so it is not listed as a party. The National Memory Base as a whole was reported in 2020 at a total investment of USD 24 billion; that figure is not recorded because it is not specific to this fab. The phase 3 fab (ymtc-wuhan-phase-3) is not linked as the same campus because no source gives its site. The Entity List date comes from Reuters reporting (s4).

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Removed Tsinghua Unigroup as an owner because it rested on a 2020 report and is outdated, recorded the 2024 production start as first production rather than volume production, widened the 2022 target to the year the source gives, and reworded the 60,000 wafers-a-month figure to match the source. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): added the August 2026 STAR Market prospectus from the Shanghai Stock Exchange as a primary source, replaced the phase 2 project company, which the prospectus says was merged into YMTC in December 2023, with the holding company as owner, added the published address and a 2025 full-output milestone, and moved the status date to the prospectus.
